sections.heading: C — State Laws and Rules
sections.markdown:
## C — State Laws and Rules

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A17
A vehicle operated on Maine public roads must be registered, insured and properly maintained. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A17
A title is the legal document identifying who owns a vehicle. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A17
A vehicle title proves ownership and records any liens, meaning debts on the vehicle. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A17
A Maine dealer supplies the blue title-application copy, which must be presented at the vehicle’s first registration. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A17
For a vehicle bought outside a Maine dealership, the buyer submits a completed title application with the prior title or manufacturer’s origin certificate properly transferred to the buyer. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A17
An owner without a lienholder receives the title; when a bank or credit union financed the purchase, that lender receives it. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A17
Store the title safely outside the vehicle. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A17
Vehicles older than 25 years are exempt from the title requirement. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A17
A trailer with an unloaded weight of 3,000 pounds or less does not need a title. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A18
Apply promptly for a duplicate if a title is stolen, lost, destroyed or mutilated. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A18
Return a mutilated or unreadable title with the duplicate application and required fee. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A18
An owner must register a motor vehicle, mobile home, trailer or semitrailer driven on Maine roads. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A18
Vehicle registration begins with payment of excise tax to the municipal tax collector. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A18
Semitrailers are exempt from the vehicle excise tax described in the manual. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A18
The vehicle’s age and factory list price determine its excise tax. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A18
The excise-tax receipt also serves as the registration application. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A18
Complete and sign the back of the white registration copy before a registration is issued. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A18
A registrant younger than 18 also needs a parent’s or guardian’s signature on the registration form. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A18
After paying excise tax, obtain registration and plates at a Motor Vehicle branch or by mailing the application and correct fee to the Bureau. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A18
Many Maine municipalities issue registrations and plates, but applicants should check whether their municipality participates. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A18
The listed passenger-vehicle registration fee is $35. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A18
A registration lasts 1 year from its month of issue. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A18
The listed pickup-registration fee is $35 when the maximum gross vehicle weight is 6,000 pounds. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A18
Registration fees for larger trucks rise as registered gross weight increases. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A18
A vehicle aged 25 years or newer needs a title application submitted at its first registration. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A18
A first Maine registration requires a Use Tax Certificate to determine whether sales tax is due. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A18
Pay any sales tax due when registering the vehicle for the first time. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A19
When a Maine auto dealer sold the vehicle, the dealer supplies the sales-tax form to present at first registration. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A19
Apply for Maine vehicle registration within 30 days after residency is declared or established. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A19
Every motor-vehicle owner and operator must maintain liability insurance and show evidence when police request it. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A19
A vehicle you drive needs insurance even when someone else owns it. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A19
Check coverage and carry insurance evidence inside the vehicle. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A19
Registering a motor vehicle in Maine requires showing insurance evidence. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A19
An insurance card, insurer or agent coverage letter, binder, or policy with the required summary can serve as insurance evidence. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A19
A policy summary used as insurance evidence identifies the vehicle, insured person, coverage type and amount, and effective and expiry dates, with amounts meeting Maine minimum liability requirements. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A19
Not producing required insurance evidence can lead to an uninsured-operation charge and loss of license and registration privileges. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A19
After adjudication for failing to produce insurance evidence, file financial-responsibility proof through an SR-22 certificate or face suspension of license and registration privileges. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A19
Displaying fabricated or altered insurance evidence is a crime. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A19
An uninsured motorist causing injury or property damage of at least $1,000 cannot drive until financial-responsibility proof or proper insurance is shown. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A19
If a court judgment is obtained after the described uninsured crash, driving and registration privileges remain suspended until the judgment is satisfied. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A19
Every Maine-written automobile liability policy includes uninsured-motorist coverage for bodily-injury damages. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A19
Required uninsured-motorist bodily-injury coverage extends to the Maine Financial Responsibility Law limits, with higher limits optional. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A19
A person unable to obtain insurance through regular channels can seek coverage through the Maine Automobile Insurance Plan. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A19
Every company selling automobile insurance in Maine must participate in the shared assigned-risk market. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

Misconceptions: insurance is required even when a driver does not own the vehicle. [A19]
Mnemonic: title, tax, registration, insurance, inspection.
Glossary: a title identifies ownership; a lien records a debt on the vehicle. [A17]
Dynamic facts: fee schedules and administrative channels require monitoring; contact details are withheld.

items.why: Ownership, registration and liability evidence impose different obligations.
Equipment thresholds and defects require separate recall and application practice.
Advisory maintenance and enforceable sound limits must remain distinct.
